description:
Start with a blank canvas and learn how to build a complete track from scratch in Suno Studio 2.0. Follow along as we explore musical typing, recording live audio, and using Studio Chat to generate synths, mix effects, and even cover your ideas into new genres.

Watch the full Studio 2.0 series here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLcGl48v5p95s

Timestamps:
00:00 - Welcome and blank canvas tour
01:34 - Musical typing with your computer keyboard
02:12 - Setting tempo and recording MIDI parts
04:56 - Applying EQ and Reverb audio effects
05:35 - Generating a new synth part with Studio Chat
08:20 - Calibrating mic latency and tracking vocals
10:02 - Recording live acoustic guitar
11:41 - Renaming tracks with Studio Chat
12:16 - Using Studio Chat to add vocal effect chains
15:08 - Using the Cover feature to reimagine your track
18:46 - Extracting stems to blend with your original project
24:07 - Playing MIDI keys and converting to a keyboard audio track
26:53 - Reversing a snare for an outro transition
27:12 - Tracking and panning additional vocal layers
30:48 - Recording a lead electric guitar solo
33:20 - Arrangement review and full song playback
35:23 - Exporting your song, multitracks, and MIDI
36:50 - Sharing your project link with collaborators
37:13 - Outro

Hosted by Henry

#SunoStudio #SunoV2 #MusicProduction #AI #DAW

comments.text:
Suno v6 may sound technically polished, but its biggest weakness is musical variety and prompt adherence.

Too often, different generations fall back to the same recognizable melodic shapes, phrasing habits, emotional character and arrangement patterns. You can significantly change the prompt, structure, mood or performance instructions, yet the model still tends to return to familiar internal templates.

Musical instructions also feel unreliable. Requests involving tempo, intensity, phrasing, dynamics, harmonic development or instrumental behavior are frequently interpreted very loosely. Increasing intensity can simply become increasing speed. Trying to control that speed can push the music too far in the opposite direction. Detailed instructions may be acknowledged in the generated description but barely reflected in the actual music.

The biggest problem is repetition. After enough generations, you start recognizing the same melodic movements, the same transitions, the same types of climaxes and the same characteristic phrases appearing again and again. Different songs can begin to feel like variations of the same underlying composition.

That seriously limits creativity. An AI music generator should not only produce high-quality audio; it should also be capable of genuinely different musical ideas.

Older models often felt more unpredictable in a positive way. They could produce surprising harmonic movement, unusual phrasing and compositions that felt more distinct from one another. v6 often sounds cleaner, but also more standardized and less adventurous.

The model does not need to behave like MIDI or follow every instruction literally. But there is a major difference between creative interpretation and repeatedly ignoring musical direction in favor of the same default patterns.

Suno should focus much more on:

• stronger prompt adherence
• greater melodic diversity
• greater harmonic diversity
• more reliable tempo control
• fewer recycled musical phrases
• less dependence on recognizable default templates
• better preservation of the musical identity requested by the user
• more genuine variation between generations

Sound quality alone is not enough.

A music-generation model also needs musical imagination, diversity and meaningful user control. Right now, v6 often feels polished on the surface but far too repetitive underneath.

comments.text:
Studio 2 has become a complete mess. It has moved so far away from the simplicity and ease of use that made the old Studio practical in the first place.

In the previous version, we could easily take an existing song and create a new cover of it. It was simple, clear, and straightforward. Now, everything is buried under so many menus, options, and unnecessary details that even something as basic as creating a new cover of a song feels almost impossible to find and use.

Why did it need to become this complicated? What was the point of adding so many unnecessary and confusing details? And more importantly, while adding all these new features, why didn’t you preserve the simple and essential functions that people were already using?

More features do not automatically mean a better experience. Sometimes simplicity is exactly what makes a tool powerful and enjoyable to use. The old Studio understood that. Studio 2 does not.

日本人さん用　たまな特化なので目的の違う人はごめんね
今のたまなのStudio 2.0の使い方に直結しそうなのは、まずこのあたり。

04:56 - Applying EQ and Reverb audio effects
→ 今日やってた「整える・音をいじる」に近い。EQやリバーブの基本を見るならここ。
05:35 - Generating a new synth part with Studio Chat
→ Studio Chatで音を足す実例。今後「この部分だけ楽器を追加したい」時に使えそう。
12:16 - Using Studio Chat to add vocal effect chains
→ ボーカル処理。声の質感や仕上げ方を見るならここ。
18:46 - Extracting stems to blend with your original project
→ これはかなり重要。 今日のBacking Vocals、笛、Drumsみたいなステム編集に直結する。
26:53 - Reversing a snare for an outro transition
→ 部分編集・加工の具体例。Studioで「こんなことまでできる」の参考。
33:20 - Arrangement review and full song playback
→ 編集後にどう全体確認してるか。
35:23 - Exporting your song, multitracks, and MIDI
→ これも重要。 Full Song / Multitrack周りの公式実演。
36:50 - Sharing your project link with collaborators
→ 今すぐ必要ではなさそう。

逆に、現状あまり優先しなくてよさそうなのは、MIDI鍵盤、マイク録音、アコギ録音、ギターソロ録音あたり。たまなが今やってる「SUNO生成曲をStudioで仕上げる」用途とは少し離れる。

だから最初は、18:46 → 35:23 → 04:56 → 12:16 の順で見るのを推す。

comments.text:
Hi Suno Team,

I have several more workflow issues and feature requests based on my recent use of Create and Studio.

### 1. Generated audio should follow the user-specified name automatically

In Studio, generated songs or music do not always use the name I specify.

This becomes very difficult to manage when one song has many versions.

Please consider adding a simple option such as:

*Use Requested Name*
or
*Auto Match Title*

When enabled, every new generated version should automatically use the requested song/project name, with an optional version suffix such as:

SongName_v01
SongName_v02
SongName_v03

This would make version management much easier and reduce the need to rename files manually afterward.

A related improvement would be:

*Rename All Related Takes to Project Name*

This could automatically align all takes, stems and alternate versions under the same naming structure.

---

### 2. Create, Studio and other Suno pages need better compatibility and shared context

Right now, different Suno pages feel too isolated from each other.

Create, Studio and GPT-assisted workflows should share more information and settings instead of acting like separate systems.

For example, when moving a song from Create into Studio, I would like Suno to preserve:

* Song name
* Prompt
* Exclude prompt
* Model version
* BPM
* Key
* Lyrics
* Structure
* Reference audio
* Style settings
* Generation history
* Track identities
* Version history

The user should not need to rebuild or re-enter the same information on every page.

---

### 3. Please add GPT directly into the normal Create page

I strongly prefer the Create page because it is much simpler and faster than Studio.

I also do not speak English well, so Studio’s more complex interface and English-only controls are difficult for me to use efficiently.

Please consider adding the same GPT-style assistant directly into the Create workflow.

The assistant should be able to help users with:

* Writing and improving prompts
* Explaining English controls
* Editing lyrics
* Building song structure
* Setting instrument hierarchy
* Setting intro / bridge / climax / outro
* Adding exclusions
* Adjusting style influence
* Reusing saved Skills or presets
* Explaining why a generation failed
* Suggesting the next generation settings

Ideally, users should be able to say something simple such as:

> Make the strings warmer, reduce harsh highs, keep the vocal clear, add a 20-second instrumental intro, and make the final climax larger.

Then GPT would automatically translate that request into the appropriate Create settings and prompt instructions.

This would save a huge amount of time, especially for users who do not understand all of the English controls.

Please also avoid unnecessarily restricting access to this type of assistant for paying users. It would make the normal Create workflow much more powerful and accessible.

---

### 4. Possible audio-quality loss after “Commit Take”

I have also noticed something that may be a quality issue.

The audio generated from the GPT-assisted generation panel on the left can sound very good.

However, after using *Commit Take* and placing that result onto the timeline on the right, I sometimes hear a noticeable reduction in audio quality.

The committed version can sound less stable, less clear, or lower quality than the version I heard before committing it.

I am still learning Studio, so I cannot yet confirm the exact technical cause, but I believe this should be investigated.

Please compare:

*Generated Preview / Take*
vs.
*Committed Timeline Take*

and verify whether Commit Take changes any of the following:

* Audio codec
* Bit depth
* Sample rate
* Loudness
* Normalization
* Resampling
* Phase
* Stereo image
* Dynamics
* Transients
* High-frequency detail
* Internal rendering quality

Ideally, *Commit Take should be bit-transparent or quality-transparent* unless a deliberate processing step is applied.

If any conversion is required, Studio should show exactly what happens.

For example:

*Original Take: 48kHz / 24-bit*
→
*Committed Take: 48kHz / 24-bit*
→
*No quality loss*

If Studio is internally rendering a lower-quality proxy for timeline playback, please make this visible and allow users to switch to full-quality playback.

---

I have many more observations and workflow ideas, but I am writing them down gradually as I discover them.

Thank you for continuing to improve Suno.
